title: Mastering UI Tab Systems
summary: This lesson details five essential rules for designing high-quality tab systems, focusing on smooth animations, accessibility, and mobile responsiveness. It covers everything from indicator motion and overflow handling to keyboard navigation and content transitions.

transcript.text: Stop letting your tabs jump. Tabs are a system.
01 Indicator. The underline slides. The underline never teleports, it slides.
Spring config matches the content fade. Slow in, fast out.
02 Overflow. 8 tabs, 1 screen. Don't wrap to a second line.
Scroll horizontal. Edge fades show what's coming. Chevron buttons on desktop.
03 Keyboard. Arrows. Home. End. Tab. Arrows move between tabs.
Home jumps first. End jumps last. Tab moves to the next focusable group.
Focus ring and active state never share a color.
04 Mobile. Mobile is different. On mobile tabs collapse.
Segmented control under 5. Bottom sheet over 5. Never just scale down the desktop version.
05 Content. Content needs to breathe. Content never cuts, fade out.
Pause 80 milliseconds. Fade in. Match the height to avoid layout shift.
Your brain reads the transition as one motion. Follow for more UI systems.

on_screen_text: EASE OUT - Slow in. Fast out.
FOCUS never the same as ACTIVE
CONTAINER HEIGHT INTERPOLATES — NO LAYOUT SHIFT
design_principles: Smooth motion over instant state changes
Visual distinction between Focus and Active states
Prevention of Layout Shift (CLS) through height interpolation
before_after: Hard-cut tab indicators and content jumping vs. smooth sliding indicators and interpolated container heights with fade transitions.
